To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. AP-3 is required to deliver PRDX6 to lamellar bodies (Lb), and 2. Lb targeting of PRDX is mediated by LIMP-2.
the loss of the AP-3 complex leads to impaired delivery of the enzyme peroxiredexin 6 (Prx6) to lamellar bodies (a lysosome-related organnelle) in alveolar type II cells.

AP-3 and LIMP-2-dependent trafficking of PRDx6 to LB is required for phospholipid degradation in LB, and that the loss of this pathway contributes to the pathogenesis of the lethal lung disease associated with HPS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathophysiology of the Hermansky Puddlak syndrome (HPS) type 2, a lysosome-related disorder of membrane trafficking.
the molecular mechanisms of membrane traffic in alveolar type II cells.
the role of lysosomal membrane proteins in the maturation and function of the surfactant system in alveolar type II cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
impaired LIM2-dependent PRDX6 delivery to lamellar bodies is a key factor in the pathogenesis of alveolar phospholipid abnormalities in HPS2 patients.

the AP-3 complex is involved in the delivery of the enzyme peroxiredexin-6 to the lamellar bodies in alveolar type II cells, and the absence of the enzyme results in an altered phospholipid composition of the lamellar bodies and a reduced degradation of disaturated phosphatylcholine in the lung.
the loss of AP3 complex function in the HPS2 model leads to a failure to deliver PRDX6 to the lamellar bodies in alveolar type II cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AP-3-dependent protein LIMP- 2/SCARB-2 facilitates the delivery of PRDX6, a peroxidase, to the LB of AT2 cells in the mouse lung.
the impaired delivery of LIMP-2 and PRDX 6 to LB in AP-3-deficient mice accounts for the accumulation of phospholipids in LB and the impaired intraluminal digestion of phospholipid in the LB.
the AP-3-dependent delivery of the soluble enzyme PRDX6 into LB is required for the maturing of the organelle and for the maintenance of the phospholipid composition of LB.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the AP-3-dependent sorting machinery in AT2 is required for normal phospholipid metabolism in the alveolus and that loss of AP-3-dependent delivery of a soluble enzyme to lamellar bodies contributes to the pathophysiology of HPS2.
the AP-3-dependent sorting of LIMP-2 to LB is essential for the normal maturation of these organelles.
the AP-3 complex is required for the delivery of the peroxidase enzyme PRDX6 to lamellar bodies (the site of surfactant phospholipid synthesis) in alveolar type II (AT2) cells.
